findings.evidence: machzor_expanded-opensiddur-he/index.xml, all 13 aliyah blocks (e.g. lines 1976-1993, 2335-2353). The Barekhu call (role_0) and the repeated response (role_3) are both labeled <note type="description" corresp="…role/reader">חזן</note>. The printed rubric says the oleh says these words, not the reader: he index line 540 / en index line 431 read 'Before reading from the Torah, the individual called upon says the following:' and 'He then repeats this and continues:'. The Codex rubric between the two labels says 'העולה חוזר על התשובה', which contradicts the חזן label right after it. ROLE_LABELS in build.py:27 has no role for the oleh, so the importer cannot express the correct speaker.
findings.action: Add a registered role for the person called up (e.g. role/oleh), use it for the call and for the repetition, and keep role/congregation for the response. Add a test that the call and the repetition are not tagged reader.

In the he index (line 566) and the en index (line 457) the editorial gap notice is an inline <tei:note type="description"> carrying the source @facs (n181/n182), even though it is Codex text and not printed on those pages. findings.evidence: build.py:447-481. qere_ketiv is one branch of an if/elif chain, so a fragment that also has uncertain_characters, abbreviations, enlarged_letters or expansion silently loses those features and gets no error. The pending 1 Sam fine readings include uncertain marks. Also, `text.count(written) != 1` / `partition` matches a substring with no word-boundary check, so a written form could bind inside a longer word. The test (test_qere_ketiv_preserves_printed_form_and_invalidates_review, lines 1236-1254) covers only the single-word case and the duplicate-span error. It does not assert that the body's printed text still equals the source, and it does not test multiple readings in order, rejection of combined features, or rejection of a partial-word match.
findings.action: Raise if qere_ketiv is combined with another fragment-level feature (or support the combination). Require a match at word boundaries (letters and points). Extend the test to assert the printed text, two ordered readings, rejection of a combined feature, and rejection of a mid-word match.

findings.evidence: build.py:314-319. end_reference_before_instructions closes active_reference but does not require the segment to open a new reference (segment['corresp']). On a continuation segment, the words after the rubric would fall outside every verse and drop silently out of verse-range transclusions. The test (test_aliyah_rubric_ends_verse_without_cutting_chapter, lines 1256-1276) checks only the positive path. It has no test for the 'requires an instruction' error, the missing-corresp case, or find_end_of_mapping of the preceding verse excluding the label.
findings.action: Raise unless the segment has a verse corresp. Add negative tests and a scope test using find_end_of_mapping.
